newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche puzzled by Moody's rating review.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche puzzled by Moody's rating review.

text.p: Germany's largest commercial bank Deutsche Bank AG, said it saw no particular reason why rating agency Moody's Investor Services planned to review its credit rating and added the bank planned to remain competitive.
Deutsche issued its statement in response to news Moody's had placed the bank's Aaa long-term debt rating and A financial strength rating under review for possible downgrade.
In the statement, a spokesman said that Moody's appeared to link the downgrade to a more difficult environment facing banks. "This matches with our assessment, which is known," the statement said.
"We cannot follow why Moody's has taken this assessment as a reason to review the ratings of Deutsche Bank and Morgan Grenfell & Co Ltd," it added.
"Deutsche Bank is convinced that it will hold its own successfully in future, even amid the tougher global competition," it continued.

Deutsche, one of the few banks in the world to carry triple-A ratings from both Moody's and its rival rating agency S & P, has been in the spotlight due to problems at its Morgan Grenfell Asset Management fund management arm.
Three of its British-based funds had to be suspended due to irregularities after the funds invested extensively in unlisted stocks, going far beyond permitted levels.
Deutsche had to pump in millions of marks of funds to absorb the unlisted securities.
S & P responded to the developments last week, saying it would monitor Deutsche closely but had taken no rating action.

In its comments earlier today, Moody's said its review would focus on the prospective impact on DB's profitability of adverse secular trends in its domestic market and the earnings volatility and business and balance-sheet risks resulting from the group's aggressive global expansion strategy.

With respect to pressures in the domestic banking market, Moody's noted that lower lending yields and higher funding costs were largely the result of growing competition among banks, flattening loan demand, and gradual savings disintermediation.
In this more difficult environment, the bank's cost structure had continued to rise, further constraining core earnings, Moody's said.
Although cyclical asset quality pressures appeared to have diminished, Moody's said the bank's provisioning needs were likely to remain higher than historic levels.
Deutsche has in recent years pursued an ambitious global expansion strategy in a bid to diversify its revenue base away from traditional net interest sources.

But Moody's said that while this growth was likely to enhance the volume of its revenues, the addition of several new business segments had increased the group's expense structure and introduced new elements of risk.
The rising scale of global competition in the financial services businesses may also strain the resources of the bank as it pursues challenging and diverse course, it said.
Moody's said it nonetheless continued to view DB as one of the strongest European financial groups.
